pin: Pass 2 asks whether the pass-1 group gap is calendar time, a higher bar for newcomers, review capacity, or a gap that remains after year controls. In-group in sections 2 and 3 is still the cumulative top 20. Section 5 replaces that with a trailing 24-month top 20. This file does not show that rejection sensitive dysphoria caused any outcome.

period_trend.note: Merge rate is among decided PRs. Open PRs are out of that denominator. Years with open share above 20% are marked right-censored and left out of the slope.

strata.effect_size_flag: negligible effect size regardless of p-value

one_year_cohorts.note: Usable stratum: at least 3 later-top-20 people and 10 leavers. MH risk difference uses Mantel-Haenszel weights n1*n0/n. PR-level MH counts decided PRs in the first year. Person-level MH treats each contributor's first-year merge rate as successes/n.

two_year_cohorts.note: Usable stratum: at least 3 later-top-20 people and 10 leavers. MH risk difference uses Mantel-Haenszel weights n1*n0/n. PR-level MH counts decided PRs in the first year. Person-level MH treats each contributor's first-year merge rate as successes/n.

cohort_control.note: The pass-1 d=0.88 is the unadjusted person-level first-year merge contrast. Fraction remaining uses the recomputed raw gap in this run, not a hardcoded 0.88, and is reported next to that pass-1 figure.

year_controlled_group_gap.sample: Decided PRs whose cumulative top-20 status is already defined. Open PRs and unidentified early PRs are excluded.

interaction.model: linear probability: outcome ~ newcomer + year_since_2010 + newcomer x year_since_2010
interaction.reading: For merge rate, a negative interaction means the incumbent advantage widens each year. For no-response, a positive interaction means newcomers go unanswered more often as years pass.

interaction.model: linear probability: outcome ~ newcomer + year_since_2010 + newcomer x year_since_2010
interaction.reading: For merge rate, a negative interaction means the incumbent advantage widens each year. For no-response, a positive interaction means newcomers go unanswered more often as years pass.

drawbridge.definition: Newcomer: this PR is within 12 months of the author's first PR. Incumbent: the author's first PR was at least 3 years earlier. Authors in between are in neither series.

rolling_ingroup.window: trailing 24 months, reviews strictly before the PR

hours_to_first_response_from_2016.effect_size_flag: negligible effect size regardless of p-value

block_a.median_comparison_note: Review-cycle medians are in the period table. This block matches pass-1 means.

peer_review_object_count_from_2016.effect_size_flag: negligible effect size regardless of p-value

justification_hits_per_pr_from_2016.effect_size_flag: negligible effect size regardless of p-value

any_negative_tone_from_2016.effect_size_flag: negligible effect size regardless of p-value

correlation_prs_per_reviewer_with_newcom.effect_note: The unit is the calendar year. The interval resamples years.

time_to_first_merge.note: Median days are among authors who eventually merged, from first PR open time to that PR's merge time. The 24-month share is among authors observable for 24 months and counts a merge only if merge time falls inside the window.

rules.universal_tightening: Weighted slope of annual decided merge rate on calendar year is entirely below 0, on years whose open share is at most 20%, and at least one of incumbent or newcomer slopes is also entirely below 0.
rules.differential_tightening_against_newcomer: The newcomer x year interaction is entirely below 0 for merge rate, or entirely above 0 for no-response rate.
rules.review_capacity_starvation: Across years, PRs per active reviewer (5+ reviews) correlates with the newcomer no-response rate and the bootstrap interval is entirely above 0.
rules.residual_group_gap_after_period_control: The in-group log-odds coefficient in the logistic model with year fixed effects, log1p(lines), files, and prior PR count has a bootstrap interval entirely above 0.

interpretation.text: These four readings can hold together. A falling merge rate for incumbents and newcomers is universal tightening. A negative newcomer-by-year interaction on top of that is differential tightening. A positive capacity correlation is starvation. An in-group coefficient that stays positive with year fixed effects is a residual group gap. None of these is a psychological finding.

INTERPRETATION
Supported: differential_tightening_against_newcomers, residual_group_gap_after_period_control
  no: universal_tightening. Weighted slope of annual decided merge rate on calendar year is entirely below 0, on years whose open share is at most 20%, and at least one of incumbent or newcomer slopes is also entirely below 0.
  yes: differential_tightening_against_newcomers. The newcomer x year interaction is entirely below 0 for merge rate, or entirely above 0 for no-response rate.
  no: review_capacity_starvation. Across years, PRs per active reviewer (5+ reviews) correlates with the newcomer no-response rate and the bootstrap interval is entirely above 0.
  yes: residual_group_gap_after_period_control. The in-group log-odds coefficient in the logistic model with year fixed effects, log1p(lines), files, and prior PR count has a bootstrap interval entirely above 0.
These four readings can hold together. A falling merge rate for incumbents and newcomers is universal tightening. A negative newcomer-by-year interaction on top of that is differential tightening. A positive capacity correlation is starvation. An in-group coefficient that stays positive with year fixed effects is a residual group gap. None of these is a psychological finding.
